- When sentiment is 0.00 across recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 65), model overweights upward momentum; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment history includes a single 0.25 (neutral bias), model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to account for latent risk.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) values; apply 1–2% downward correction to final 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows a sustained upward trend (e.g., 5+ consecutive days above 67), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
